observations:
Torah LM2/86 is one of the most compact Torahs in Likutay Moharan — five lines that develop a single linear argument about the ruach/emunah spectrum. The teaching has no sub-arguments, digressions, or independent conceptual domains beyond the three already captured in the package analysis.

The entire Torah operates within one conceptual axis: the presence or absence of ruach (spirit) as a measure of faith. Three packages cover this axis completely:
- Package 1 (good): complete faith = long spirit
- Package 2 (failing): little faith = short spirit
- Package 3 (evil): idolatry/heresy = no spirit

The structural analogy used in lines 2 and 4 (שעת שמד) introduces a parallel case to illustrate how the level of faith-deficiency determines the level of required avodah. This analogy does not introduce an independent conceptual domain with its own bechina network — it is a mashal (parable/analogy) deployed in an eitza capacity to argue from the extreme case (total shemad = martyrdom required) toward the milder case (קטני אמנה = harsh avodah required). No bechina language is used to equate שמד with a spiritual concept in the domain of the packages.

The final line (line 5) introducing 'כמה בחינות בקטני אמנה' (several sub-levels of little faith) and citing the midrash on 'מי גרם לצדיקים' could suggest an independent 'levels of faith' package — but the text is truncated at exactly this point (ending with 'וכו' indicating continuation not preserved in the file). The sub-levels are merely varieties within Package 2, not an independent domain. No bechina equatings are stated for these sub-levels in the extant text.

Conclusion: the three packages fully capture the bechina topology of Torah LM2/86 as it stands. No additional independent domain with 3+ explicitly bechina-connected concepts exists in this text.
